overall: No current observations are available for Atlanta, leaving the forecast entirely model-driven as of this analysis. The NWS has issued a Heat Advisory through 8 PM EDT for portions of central and east central Georgia, with heat index values of 105–108°F expected — consistent with a hot, humid airmass in place. Conditions are forecast to remain mostly sunny through the afternoon with only a slight late-day storm threat (20% PoP after 4 PM) that could briefly clip the high.
forecast_obs_notes: The four NWP models show meaningful spread: GFS is an outlier at 96.3°F while ECMWF (93.0°F), HRRR (91.3°F), and NBM (90.5°F) cluster in a tighter 91–93°F range; the NWS text forecast of 'near 93°F' closely matches ECMWF and lies near the top of the model consensus band, suggesting the GFS hot bias should be discounted. The D1_NOW probability distribution reflects this spread, with mass concentrated in the 90–95°F zone and the peak even bucket at 92–93°F (8.3%), indicating no single outcome dominates.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely TMAX today falls in the 92–94°F range, anchored by the NWS text forecast of 93°F and supported by ECMWF agreement; the GFS 96.3°F solution appears to be an outlier and is not well-supported by the ensemble or NBM. The active even-bucket market top is 92–93°F at only 8.3% probability — a very flat distribution — and ensemble signals rate this Tier 4 (Avoid) with a no_trade abort, reflecting genuine model uncertainty across a wide spread. Confidence is moderate-low given the ~5.8°F model range and absence of any intraday observations to anchor the forecast.
